docker-fundamentals-sr1-08.reason: ambiguous: by default the CLI does use the local dockerd socket, so an expert could defend True. The new wording tests the remote-daemon fact directly (final: fixed)
docker-fundamentals-sr1-08.statement: With the active docker context pointing at a remote host's daemon, `docker ps` lists the local machine's containers.
docker-fundamentals-sr1-08.explanation: The CLI sends each command to the daemon chosen by -H, DOCKER_HOST or the active docker context, which can be a remote host reached over SSH or TCP. With none of these set, it uses the local daemon socket.
docker-fundamentals-sr1-08.misconception: The docker CLI can talk only to a daemon on its own host.

docker-fundamentals-sr3-12.reason: ambiguous: the reference shows a RUN heredoc (cat > file1) whose lines end up as files, so True was defensible. The card now tests the COPY side (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr3-12.statement: `COPY <<EOF /app.sh` runs the heredoc lines in the default shell during the build.
docker-fundamentals-sr3-12.explanation: A COPY heredoc writes the here-document content to the destination file, here /app.sh. A RUN heredoc with no command is the form the default shell executes.
docker-fundamentals-sr3-12.misconception: A COPY heredoc executes its lines like a RUN heredoc.

docker-fundamentals-sr5-03.reason: source_problem: no official page supports the clause 'even when that stage has a name'. It is removed so the multi-stage page supports the whole card (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr5-03.statement: `COPY --from=0` copies from the stage that the first FROM instruction in the Dockerfile starts.
docker-fundamentals-sr5-03.explanation: Unnamed stages are referenced by integer, starting at 0 for the first FROM. Naming stages with AS keeps COPY --from working if the stages are reordered later.

docker-fundamentals-sr5-04.reason: weak_card, rewritten because dropping it with the other three weak r5 cards would leave 8 cards. It now tests the external-image pull behaviour. The page says 'The Docker client pulls the image if necessary and copies the artifact from there' (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr5-04.statement: A build with `COPY --from=nginx:latest` stops with an error when nginx:latest is missing locally.
docker-fundamentals-sr5-04.explanation: When --from names an image instead of a stage, Docker pulls that image if necessary during the build and copies the file from it.
docker-fundamentals-sr5-04.misconception: COPY --from can only use an external image that was pulled beforehand.

docker-fundamentals-sr6-11.reason: weak_card (the flag name gives it away), rewritten because dropping all four weak r6 cards would leave 8 cards at 3/5. Backends page: 'In min cache mode (the default), only layers that are exported into the resulting image are cached' (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr6-11.statement: With its default mode, `--cache-to` exports cache only for layers that end up in the final image.
docker-fundamentals-sr6-11.explanation: The default mode=min caches only layers exported into the resulting image; mode=max also caches the layers of intermediate steps, for more cache hits.

docker-fundamentals-sr7-07.reason: weak_card (strawman about the image store), rewritten because r7 would otherwise fall below 9 cards. Login page: without a credential store, credentials go into config.json 'in a base64-encoded format' (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr7-07.statement: When `docker login` saves credentials directly to `config.json`, it encrypts them first.
docker-fundamentals-sr7-07.explanation: Without a credential store, Docker writes credentials to config.json only base64-encoded, which anyone can reverse. A credential store keeps them in an external store such as the OS keychain or pass.
docker-fundamentals-sr7-07.misconception: config.json holds registry credentials in encrypted form.

docker-fundamentals-sr7-08.reason: weak_card (the flag name gives it away), rewritten because r7 would otherwise fall below 9 cards. Push page: to push to a self-hosted registry, 'tag the image with the host name or IP address, and the port of the registry' (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr7-08.statement: `docker image push` takes its destination registry from the host part of the image reference.
docker-fundamentals-sr7-08.explanation: To publish to a self-hosted registry, you first tag the image as host:port/name, and Docker pushes to the registry named in that reference.

docker-fundamentals-sr8-02.reason: weak_card (repeats the same-path sharing template), rewritten because r8 would otherwise drop to 7 cards. Volumes page: 'Anonymous volumes are given a random name that's guaranteed to be unique within a given Docker host' (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr8-02.statement: When a container creates an anonymous volume, Docker names that volume after the container.
docker-fundamentals-sr8-02.explanation: Docker gives an anonymous volume a random name that is unique on that Docker host. docker inspect shows it in the container's Mounts section.
docker-fundamentals-sr8-02.misconception: An anonymous volume takes the name of the container that created it.

docker-fundamentals-sr8-09.reason: weak_card (near-truism), rewritten because r8 would otherwise drop to 7 cards. The volumes page shows volume-driver=local with volume-opt=type=nfs, device and addr (final: fixed)
docker-fundamentals-sr8-09.statement: On Linux, Docker's built-in `local` volume driver mounts NFS exports as volumes through its volume options.
docker-fundamentals-sr8-09.explanation: The local driver passes mount options from volume-opt, for example type=nfs with addr and device, so an NFS share needs no third-party volume plugin.

docker-fundamentals-sr10-11.reason: weak_card (the flag syntax and the hedge verb 'lets' give it away), rewritten because r10 would otherwise drop to 8 cards at 3/5. The networking overview's Redis example binds to 127.0.0.1 and connects from a container:redis peer (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr10-11.statement: With `--network container:redis`, a container reaches Redis bound to 127.0.0.1 inside `redis`.
docker-fundamentals-sr10-11.explanation: The container: mode joins the other container's network stack, loopback included, so a service bound to localhost in one container is reachable from the other.

docker-fundamentals-sr11-04.reason: ambiguous: COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME beats the top-level name even when no -p is given. The card now tests that precedence, from the project-name page (final: fixed)
docker-fundamentals-sr11-04.statement: `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` takes precedence over the top-level `name` in a Compose file.
docker-fundamentals-sr11-04.explanation: Compose takes the project name from the -p flag first, then COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, then the top-level name, and then the base name of the project directory.

docker-fundamentals-sr12-04.reason: weak_card (the name privileged gives it away), rewritten because r12 would otherwise drop to 7 cards. Run page: --privileged 'gives all capabilities', 'enables access to all devices on the host, and reconfigures AppArmor or SELinux' (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr12-04.statement: `docker run --cap-add=ALL` gives a container the same access to the host as `--privileged`.
docker-fundamentals-sr12-04.explanation: Beyond granting all capabilities, --privileged opens access to all host devices and reconfigures AppArmor or SELinux; --cap-add=ALL only adds capabilities.
docker-fundamentals-sr12-04.misconception: --privileged only adds capabilities, so --cap-add=ALL is equivalent.

docker-fundamentals-sr12-07.reason: weak_card (it restates the instruction's name), rewritten because r12 would otherwise drop to 7 cards, and to keep USER coverage. Run page: 'you can override the USER instruction by passing the -u option' (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr12-07.statement: `docker run --user 1000` overrides the user named by the image's USER.
docker-fundamentals-sr12-07.explanation: USER sets the default user for the image's first process, and the -u or --user option of docker run replaces it for that container.

docker-fundamentals-sr3-05.reason: tell: removes 'remain' (persistence verbs appeared only in false statements). Same fact and answer (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr3-05.statement: A container started from the image sees the Dockerfile's ARG values as environment variables.
docker-fundamentals-sr3-05.explanation: ARG supplies build-time values. ENV sets environment values that persist in the built image.
docker-fundamentals-sr3-05.misconception: ARG persists as a runtime environment variable like ENV.

docker-fundamentals-sr6-06.reason: tell: removes 'keeps' and 'stays' (false-only words). Same fact and answer (final: fixed)
docker-fundamentals-sr6-06.statement: After one RUN step misses the cache, BuildKit reuses cache for later RUN steps in that stage with unchanged text.
docker-fundamentals-sr6-06.explanation: Once a step misses the cache, later RUN steps in that stage rebuild even with unchanged text, because each runs on the previous step's result.
docker-fundamentals-sr6-06.misconception: Later RUN steps remain cached as long as their command strings stay the same.

docker-fundamentals-sr10-01.reason: tell: removes the 'On Linux' prefix (the platform prefix marked false 8 times out of 12). Same fact and answer; Linux is the deck's default scope (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr10-01.statement: By default, `docker run` creates a new bridge network for the container it starts.
docker-fundamentals-sr10-01.explanation: Without a network option, Docker Engine connects the container to the built-in default `bridge` network.
docker-fundamentals-sr10-01.misconception: Docker creates a separate bridge network for each new container.

docker-fundamentals-sr10-10.reason: tell: removes the 'On Linux' prefix. Same fact and answer (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr10-10.statement: `ipvlan` L2 mode assigns containers MAC addresses distinct from the parent interface.
docker-fundamentals-sr10-10.explanation: In `ipvlan` L2 mode, containers use the parent interface's MAC address. The `macvlan` driver assigns a MAC address to each container interface.
docker-fundamentals-sr10-10.misconception: IPvlan L2 exposes a separate container MAC address to the physical network.

docker-fundamentals-sr12-02.reason: tell: removes the 'On Linux' prefix. Same fact and answer (final: keep)
docker-fundamentals-sr12-02.statement: With userns-remap enabled in daemon.json, the Docker daemon runs as a non-root host user.
docker-fundamentals-sr12-02.explanation: With `userns-remap`, container root maps to an unprivileged host UID, but the daemon still runs as root. Rootless mode runs both without root privileges.
docker-fundamentals-sr12-02.misconception: User namespace remapping makes the daemon itself rootless.
